question.worked_solution:
First, remember that a fraction represents a division.  So, a fraction of fractions is a division of two fractions:

$$
\frac{\,(-\frac{5}{4})\,}{(-\frac{1}{8})}=(-\frac{5}{4})÷(-\frac{1}{8})
$$

Now, recall that dividing by $-\frac{1}{8}$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $-\frac{8}{1}.$ We can use this fact to simplify the fraction above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}(-\frac{5}{4})÷(-\frac{1}{8}) & = \\ (-\frac{5}{4})\times (-\frac{8}{1}) & = \\ \frac{5\times 8}{4\times 1} & = \\ \frac{40}{4} & = \\ 10\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{\,(-\frac{5}{4})\,}{(-\frac{1}{8})}=10.
$$
